questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, Il and IlI. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All computers are laptops. All laptops are mobiles. Some mobiles are tablets. Conclusions: I. Some mobiles are computers. II. All computers are mobiles. III. Some computers are tablets.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, Il and IlI. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All computers are laptops.

All laptops are mobiles.

Some mobiles are tablets.

Conclusions:

I. Some mobiles are computers.

II. All computers are mobiles.

III. Some computers are tablets.

options.text: Only conclusions Il and III follow.
options.html: Only conclusions Il and III follow.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
I. Some mobiles are computers → Follow (As, all computers are laptops and all laptops are mobiles. So, as whole computers comes in laptops which whole comes in mobiles therefore it is definitely true.)

II. All computers are mobiles → Follow (As, all computers are laptops and all laptops are mobiles. So, as whole computers comes in laptops which whole comes in mobiles therefore it is definitely true.)

III. Some computers are tablets → Does not Follow (As, all laptops are mobiles and some mobiles are tablets . So, it is possible but not definitely true.)

Here, Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about unemployment in India: a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas. b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India. c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy. Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about unemployment in India:

a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas.

b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India.

c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.

Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Correct choice: c) Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can reduce rural unemployment by providing continuous work for agricultural laborers. Choice a) is inaccurate as Seasonal Unemployment occurs in rural areas due to monsoon-based agriculture, not urban. Choice b) is incorrect as Educated Unemployment is linked to urban regions with more education and job-seeking in industrial or service sectors.

questions.question: The folk dance of Kummi is performed by the women of which Indian state?
questions.questionHtml: The folk dance of Kummi is performed by the women of which Indian state?
questions.solution: The Kummi dance is a popular folk dance in the state of Tamil Nadu, particularly in rural areas. It is primarily performed by women, often in a circle, holding each other's hands or waists, but men also sometimes participate. There are different styles of Kummi, such as Poonthatti Kummi, Deepa Kummi (with lamps in hand), and Kulavai Kummi (performed by washerwomen).

questions.question: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is ______.
questions.questionHtml: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is ______.
questions.solution: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is justiciable. Meaning, the rights included in Part III of the Indian Constitution (which contain the fundamental rights of Indian citizens) are legally enforceable by the courts. This contrasts with the fundamental duties, which are moral obligations for all citizens but are not legally enforced by the court of law.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.solution: "Problem in storage" is not related to the function of money. Actually, part of the benefit of money is that it eliminates the storage issue inherent in a barter system. Money doesn’t physically deteriorate and could be stored or saved for future use with ease.

questions.question: ______ is a naturally occurring organic compound with the formula (C 6 H 5 ) 2 CO.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is a naturally occurring organic compound with the formula (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CO.
questions.solution: The organic compound with the formula (C6H5)2CO is Benzophenone. It consists of two phenyl groups attached to a carbonyl. Benzophenone is a white, crystalline solid and is slightly soluble in water but can dissolve in many organic solvents.

questions.question: What is the priority zone of the AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) mission, which was launched by the Government of India in 2015?
questions.questionHtml: What is the priority zone of the AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) mission, which was launched by the Government of India in 2015?
questions.solution: The Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) was launched by the Indian government in 2015 with a primary focus on establishing and upgrading infrastructure in cities and towns across the country. The topmost priority is given to water supply projects, ensuring every household has access to a tap with a supply of water and a sewerage connection.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Harijan Sevak Sangh founded in 1932?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the founder of Harijan Sevak Sangh founded in 1932?
questions.solution: The All India Harijan Sevak Sangh, founded in 1932 after Gandhi's fast and Poona Pact, fights untouchability. Born from Gandhi's opposition to British division tactics, it aimed to unite Hindus against discrimination. The Harijan paper spread this message. "Harijan" means "children of God" for untouchables.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following rulers did Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveller, come to India?
questions.questionHtml: During the reign of which of the following rulers did Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveller, come to India?
questions.solution: Hiuen Tsang travelled to India in the 7th Century CE, during the reign of Harshavardhana. His main objective was to acquire Buddhist texts which were not available in his homeland, China. He also intended to study the language and culture of India, something he was deeply fascinated with.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.solution: Article 79 of the Indian Constitution establishes the bicameral nature of the Indian Parliament, consisting of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), the Lok Sabha (House of the People), and the President of India. This ensures a two-house legislative system in the country.

questions.question: Which sodium compound is the most popular additive to various items such as sauces, salad dressings and beverages for Its preservative action?
questions.questionHtml: Which sodium compound is the most popular additive to various items such as sauces, salad dressings and beverages for Its preservative action?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sodium benzoate.

Key PointsSodium benzoate is the sodium compound most commonly used as a preservative in items such as sauces, salad dressings, and beverages. Its excellent antimicrobial characteristics help extend the shelf life of foods and beverages.

 Additional Information

  • Sodium bicarbonate - Commonly known as baking soda, is primarily used in baking as a leavening agent.
  • Sodium fluoride - It's widely used in toothpaste and drinking water to prevent tooth decay.
  • Sodium hypochlorite - This is the active ingredient in bleach and is commonly used for disinfection and water treatment.

questions.solution: In a landmark ruling on June 28, 2021 (State of Kerala vs Leesamma Joseph case), the Supreme Court of India affirmed that persons with disabilities have the right to reservation in job promotions under Article 16(4) of the Constitution. This extends to both public and private sectors, ensuring equality of opportunity as well as inclusion in the workforce. The decision also validated the relevance of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, in ensuring such reservations.

questions.question: In the Olympic flag, the total number of rings are _______.
questions.questionHtml: In the Olympic flag, the total number of rings are _______.
questions.solution: The Olympic flag features five interlaced rings: blue, yellow, black, green, and red. These rings symbolize unity among the five continents - America (North and South as one), Africa, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. The interlacing represents global athlete unity. Adopted in 1914, it flew in 1920's Olympics, signifying international togetherness.

questions.question: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi?
questions.solution: Ziauddin Barani is the author of the historical text "Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi." This book is a chronicle of the reign of Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq, a ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty in Delhi Sultanate. It provides valuable insights into the political and social aspects of that period.

questions.question: The Desh Ke Mentor Programme la launched by the Delhi government in October 2021 is for the students of classes ________.

questions.solution: The "Desh Ke Mentor Programme" was launched by the Delhi government in October 2021 to provide mentorship and guidance to students of classes 9 to 12. The program aims to support students in making informed career choices and preparing for competitive exams.

questions.question: The Hemis Festival is widely celebrated in which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: The Hemis Festival is widely celebrated in which of the following?

questions.solution:
(12 M + 16 B) × 5 = (13 M + 24 B) × 4 ⇒ 60 M - 52 M = 96 B - 80 B ⇒ M/B = 2/1

Total work = (12 M + 16 B) × 5 ⇒ (24 + 16) × 5 = 40 × 5 = 200 units

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "exploitation".

Key Points

  • "Exploitation" means making use of something for one's own benefit or advantage.
  • In the given context, it refers to making use of resources or opportunities.
  • Grammatically, it is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3".

Additional Information

  • Safeguarding: protecting something from harm or danger.
  • Preservation: keeping something in its original state or condition.
  • Migration: movement of people or animals from one place to another.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "monitoring."
 Key Points
  • "Monitoring" means keeping track of something and making sure it's running smoothly.
  • Grammatically, it fits the blank in the sentence: "Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4, neglecting, monitoring, overlooking, forgetting..."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Additional Information

  • Neglecting: means ignoring or not paying attention to something.
  • Overlooking: means missing something that should have been seen or noticed.
  • Forgetting: means not remembering something that was previously known.
  • Neglecting, overlooking, and forgetting all have negative connotations and imply that something important was missed or ignored.
  • Monitoring, on the other hand, implies being proactive and taking steps to prevent problems.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "recreational".
Key Points
  • The word "recreational" (मनोरंजन) means something that is done for enjoyment or leisure.
  • It is the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
    • Example: She went on a recreational trip to the beach with her friends.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Additional Information

  • Arduous (कठिन) means something that requires a lot of effort or is difficult.
  • Work-related(काम से संबंधित) means something that is related to one's job or profession.
  • Strenuous (ज़ोरदार) means something that requires physical exertion or effort.
